title:
Energy 
Bites
ingredients: 1 cup rolled oats (use certified gluten‑free oats if needed)
½ cup natural peanut butter (or sunflower seed butter for nut‑free)
⅓ cup honey or maple syrup
¼ cup mini dark chocolate chips (optional)
substitutions: Replace peanut butter with sunflower seed butter for those with nut allergies.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine oats, peanut (or seed) butter, and honey.
Stir in chocolate chips, chia seeds, and shredded coconut if using.
Mix well until all ingredients are evenly combined.
Scoop out small portions (about 1 tablespoon each) and roll into balls using your hands.
Place the energy bites on a parchment-lined tray and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
mealPreppingTip: Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to one week.

title: Veggie Chips with Guacamole
ingredients: 1 bunch kale (or substitute with thinly sliced zucchini)
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Remove kale leaves from the stems, tear into bite-size pieces, and toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Arrange in a single layer on a baking sheet and bake for 10–15 minutes until crisp (keep an eye to prevent burning).
In a bowl, mash the avocado with lime juice. Mix in chopped tomato, salt, and pepper. Optionally add a pinch of cumin or paprika for extra flavor.
Serve the freshly baked veggie chips with a side of guacamole for dipping.
mealPreppingTip: Bake a batch of chips and store in a sealed container for a couple of days. Prepare the guacamole fresh to avoid browning, or store the mashed avocado with a little extra lime juice and a thin layer of olive oil on top.

title:
Homemade 
Popcorn
ingredients: Optional: Nutritional yeast, smoked paprika, or a dash of cayenne pepper for extra flavor
instructions: In a large heavy pot with a lid, heat the oil over medium-high heat.
Add a few kernels and cover; when they pop, add the remaining kernels in an even layer.
Cover the pot, shake occasionally, and remove from heat once the popping slows (about 2–3 seconds between pops).
Transfer the popcorn to a large bowl, and while still warm, sprinkle with salt and your chosen flavorings.
mealPreppingTip: Popcorn is best enjoyed fresh for maximum crunch; however, store any leftovers in an airtight container for up to one day.

title: Apple Slices with Almond Butter
ingredients: 1 crisp apple (any variety), cored and sliced
2–3 tbsp almond butter (or sunflower seed butter for nut-free)
substitutions: Swap almond butter with sunflower seed butter for nut allergies.
instructions: Core and slice the apple into wedges or thin rounds.
Spread a dollop of almond butter on each slice.
Optionally sprinkle a bit of cinnamon on top for extra flavor.
mealPreppingTip: To prevent browning, lightly drizzle the apple slices with lemon juice and store in an airtight container in the fridge. Enjoy within the same day for best texture.

title:
Roasted 
Chickpeas
ingredients: ½ tsp ground cumin (or your favorite spice blend)
instructions: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
Pat the chickpeas dry with paper towels. In a bowl, toss with olive oil, salt, pepper, and cumin.
Spread the chickpeas on a baking sheet in a single layer.
Roast for 20–30 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the chickpeas are crispy.
Allow to cool completely before transferring to an airtight container.
mealPreppingTip: Store in a sealed container for up to 3 days for a crunchy, protein-packed snack.

title:
Cucumber & Hummus 
Bites
ingredients: ½ cup hummus (choose your favorite flavor)
A pinch of paprika or chopped fresh parsley for garnish
substitutions: Substitute hummus with a bean-based dip if needed.
instructions: Wash and slice the cucumber into ½‑inch rounds.
Top each slice with about a teaspoon of hummus.
Sprinkle lightly with paprika or garnish with parsley.
mealPreppingTip: Assemble fresh when ready to eat; if prepping ahead, store the cucumber slices and hummus separately and assemble just before serving to maintain crunch.

title:
Yogurt and Berry 
 Bark
ingredients: 2 cups plain Greek yogurt (or plant‑based yogurt for dairy‑free)
1 cup mixed fresh berries (blueberries, raspberries, chopped strawberries)
Optional: A handful of granola for crunch
substitutions: Use non-dairy yogurt for a vegan or dairy‑free option.
instructions: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Spread the yogurt evenly over the paper to about ¼‑inch thickness.
Drizzle honey or maple syrup over the yogurt and gently swirl with a knife.
Scatter the berries evenly on top; add granola if using.
Place in the freezer for at least 2–3 hours until completely firm.
Once frozen, break the yogurt bark into pieces.
mealPreppingTip: Keep any leftover bark wrapped tightly in the freezer for a cool, refreshing snack.

title:
Mini Veggie 
Frittata Bites
ingredients: 6 eggs (or egg substitute/flax egg for vegan)
Optional: ¼ cup shredded cheese (or dairy‑free alternative)
substitutions: Use egg replacer and omit or swap cheese for a dairy‑free version.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a bowl, whisk the eggs with salt and pepper. Stir in the chopped spinach, bell peppers, onion, and cheese if using.
Pour the mixture into a greased mini muffin tin, filling each about ¾ full.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the frittata bites are set and slightly golden on top.
Allow to cool before removing from the tin.
mealPreppingTip: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator. Reheat in the microwave for 20–30 seconds when ready to eat.

title:
Cheese & Cracker 
Bites
ingredients: A selection of whole grain or gluten‑free crackers
Sliced cheese of your choice (cheddar, Swiss, or dairy‑free alternatives)
Optional: Fresh grapes or apple slices for an extra pop of flavor
substitutions: Choose dairy‑free cheese and gluten‑free crackers if needed.
instructions: Arrange the crackers on a plate.
Place a slice of cheese on each cracker.
Optionally, top with a slice of apple or grape for added texture and natural sweetness.
mealPreppingTip: Pack crackers and cheese separately if preparing ahead; assemble just before serving to keep the crackers crisp.

title:
Rice Cake Snacks
 with Avocado
ingredients: Optional: A squeeze of lime and slices of tomato
instructions: In a bowl, mash the avocado with salt, pepper, and a squeeze of lime juice if desired.
Spread a generous layer of mashed avocado on each rice cake.
Top with thin slices of tomato if using.
mealPreppingTip: Assemble fresh to retain the crisp texture of rice cakes. Pre-slice avocado and add a little lemon juice in an airtight container, then spread over the rice cakes right before eating.

title:
Nut‑Free Banana 
Bread Muffins
ingredients: 2 eggs (or flax eggs for a vegan alternative)
substitutions: Ensure the flour blend is nut‑free.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
In a bowl, combine the mashed bananas, eggs, vanilla extract, and honey.
In a separate bowl, mix the gluten‑free flour, baking soda, and salt.
Stir the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients until just combined.
Spoon the batter into a greased or lined muffin tin.
Bake for 15–20 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
mealPreppingTip: Allow muffins to cool completely before storing in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title:
Crispy Seaweed 
Snacks
ingredients: A light spritz of olive oil or sesame oil
instructions: Preheat your oven to 275°F (135°C).
Lightly brush each seaweed sheet with oil, then sprinkle with a pinch of salt.
Place on a baking sheet in a single layer and bake for about 10 minutes until crisp (check frequently to prevent burning).
Let cool completely before breaking into bite‑size pieces.
mealPreppingTip: Store in an airtight container to retain crispness.

title: Frozen Fruit Pops
ingredients: 2 cups fresh fruit (e.g., banana slices, berries, mango chunks)
½ cup fruit juice or water (adjust for desired consistency)
Optional: 1–2 tsp honey or maple syrup
instructions: In a blender, combine the fruit, juice (or water), and sweetener until smooth.
Pour the mixture into popsicle molds or small paper cups, inserting a popsicle stick in the center.
Freeze for at least 4 hours or overnight until solid.
mealPreppingTip: Make a large batch and store in the freezer for a refreshing, healthy treat.

title: Trail Mix Clusters
ingredients: 1 cup gluten‑free cereal or puffed rice
½ cup dried cranberries or raisins
substitutions: Adjust seeds and dried fruit as needed for specific dietary requirements.
instructions: In a bowl, mix together the cereal, dried fruit, seeds, and chocolate chips (if using).
Drizzle the honey over the mixture and stir until the ingredients are well coated.
Spread the mixture onto a parchment-lined baking sheet, pressing it lightly into a compact layer.
Refrigerate for about 1–2 hours until clusters firm up, then break into bite‑size pieces.
mealPreppingTip: Store clusters in an airtight container in the fridge for a crunchy snack.

title: No‑Bake Oat Bars
ingredients: 1½ cups rolled oats (use gluten‑free oats if preferred)
½ cup peanut butter or sunflower seed butter
⅓ cup honey or maple syrup
¼ cup dried fruit (like raisins or cranberries)
Optional: 2 tbsp cocoa nibs or shredded coconut
substitutions: Use sunflower seed butter for a nut‑free version.
instructions: In a medium bowl, mix together the peanut (or seed) butter and honey until smooth.
Stir in the oats, dried fruit, and any optional ingredients until well combined.
Press the mixture firmly into a lined baking pan.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until it sets.
Cut into bars or squares.
mealPreppingTip: Keep the oat bars refrigerated in an airtight container for grab‑and‑go convenience throughout the week.
